formal_statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (g : (Fin n → Bool) → Bool), (∃ y y' : Fin n → Bool, g y ≠ g y') → (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize (n + 1) (fun x : Fin (n + 1) → Bool => xor (x (Fin.last n)) (g (fun i : Fin n => x i.castSucc))) (s + 4) ↔ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize n g s ∨ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize n (fun y : Fin n → Bool => !(g y)) s))
plain_statement: For a non-constant Boolean function g on n inputs and every s: the function x_last XOR g (first n inputs) on n + 1 inputs has a circuit of AND, OR (fan-in two) and NOT gates with at most s + 4 gates exactly when g or NOT g has such a circuit with at most s gates.
title: XOR with a fresh input costs exactly four gates over the cheaper of a function and its negation
